jurisdictions.name: Lincoln / Lancaster County
jurisdictions.office: Lincoln Planning and Development Services, Building and Safety
notes: Building permit applications are made through the Citizen Access portal.
Lincoln's Water Quality page says a family pool that can hold 18 inches of water or more must be enclosed by a fence or wall at least four feet high.
For a pool built wholly or partly above ground, the part of the pool wall that sits above ground may count toward that four-foot enclosure height.

Lincoln's homeowner electrical page says swimming pools and hot tubs, with any associated building construction, must be permitted and done by an electrical contractor, not under the homeowner permit.
Only the owner of a detached single-family home can apply for a homeowner electrical permit, and the applicant must currently live there.

jurisdictions.name: Sarpy County (unincorporated areas)
notes: Sarpy County handles zoning and building outside municipal limits and extraterritorial jurisdiction.
Projects inside Papillion, Gretna, Bellevue, Springfield or La Vista go to that city instead.
Building permits are applied for online in the county's permitting system, which is powered by SmartGov.
The county lists a separate operating permit for public swimming pools and spas; the permit page reviewed has no residential pool detail.

jurisdictions.name: Bellevue
notes: Unless exempted, separate plumbing, mechanical and electrical permits are required in addition to the building permit.
The city's FAQ lists prefabricated pools at a single-family home as exempt from a building permit only if the walls are entirely above adjacent grade and capacity is 5,000 gallons or less.
Under Section 9.09.08, a pool wider than 9 feet and deeper than 18 inches needs a 6-foot privacy or chain-link fence with a self-closing, self-latching gate.

jurisdictions.name: Papillion (Sarpy County)
jurisdictions.office: City of Papillion Building & Fire Safety
jurisdictions.portal_name: Online Building Permit Portal (Accela Citizen Access)
notes: The city's Pools (Above and In Ground) page says a site plan is required with your online permit submittal; you choose your lot type and fill in the pool site plan form for a corner lot or an interior lot.
Papillion's accessory use building permit application covers in-ground and above-ground swimming pools and asks for the pool's length, width, maximum water depth and capacity in gallons.

The application requires an accurate site plan showing the project location on the lot with dimensions, including set-back distances from the edge of the project to the rear and side property lines and the distance to the existing residence.
The application says separate permits are required for electrical, mechanical or plumbing work.
